statement: By steps 100-400, RL-Zero-Math has mainly taught the base to open and run in RL's long 'Okay' deliberation mode, the same mode the opening cue forces. Its per-token sharpness stays at the cued base's level, with no early entropy collapse. The extra T 0.6 cap hits are therefore the cued base's own loops (the base cannot sustain long deliberation), not top-p locks caused by a lower-entropy policy. Truncation negatives remove them later.
why_strongest: Every measured value fits, and the advocate accepts the mode switch (0.65 'Okay' openers at step 100, cue adding little at step 400, finished length about 1.8x). The two readings now differ only on the theory's causal step: a sharper, lower-entropy policy. The rival does without it. (1) Step 100 cap hits (+0.076, about 103) land just under the cued base's 119 (result-e870a1), although step 100 sits at the weight noise floor (knowledge-9c5052) and its activations on RL text barely move (RLN-2 step_0100 r 0.989-0.9999, knowledge-87618d). A change in the opening (8-12 nats of KL at the cue positions, against 0.06-0.09 nats per token after it even at step 2,800, result-fdc8da) produces that jump. A collapse of per-token entropy cannot happen while the weights stay this close to the base. (2) Step 400 (+0.066) shows no further rise, as a one-time switch implies. Under progressive sharpening it should grow. (3) Harder-set +0.070 and the 0.80 loop share match the cued base's loop profile (92/119 low-ratio cap hits, knowledge-787e53; 173 cued cap hits on hard328 at T 0.6). (4) The cued base's loops are fixed by a sound prefix or a restart (knowledge-1497e8), so they are failures to sustain deliberation, not sharpness. The theory's import of a 73 % early entropy drop (2505.22617) comes from Qwen-style runs and has never been measured on this pair.

tests.experiment: Per-token sharpness of RL step-100 finished answers relative to the cued base: share of step-100 plain finished answers whose mean_logprob exceeds the median mean_logprob of the cued base's finished answers, MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
tests.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (R, reference) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (X). In each file keep rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in both files (set S). In each file, finished rows = rows in S with cap_hit false (if cap_hit is missing, finished only if finish_reason == 'stop'). Drop rows whose mean_logprob field is missing, null or non-finite. Let M = median of mean_logprob over R's finished rows (even count: mean of the two middle values). Statistic: (number of X finished rows with mean_logprob strictly greater than M) / (number of X finished rows). Ties with M count as not greater. Cap-hit rows are excluded from both files.
tests.theory_should_say: The advocate puts most of the entropy drop before step 100. A sharper step-100 policy should then sit well above the cued base per token, around 0.75-0.85 of its finished answers above the cued-base median. The rival keeps step 100's per-token sharpness at the cued base's level (about 0.5), because only the opening mode changed.

tests.theory_should_say: With most of the entropy collapse done by step 200 (2505.22617), the theory puts step 400 most of the way to step 2,800 in per-token sharpness, about 0.75-0.9. The rival puts it near the cued base, about 0.25, because steps 100-400 changed the mode and left the per-token distribution alone.
